title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies distinct molecular and phenotypic ALS subtypes in post-mortem motor cortex and blood expression data
summary: Non-smooth nonnegative matrix factorization of post-mortem motor-cortex expression data identified three molecular subgroups in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, with distinct molecular and clinical patterns. Signature assignment was evaluated in separate TargetALS and blood datasets, but this does not establish prospective clinical subtyping.
ai_technology: Unsupervised non-smooth nonnegative matrix factorization derives expression clusters; linear discriminant models transfer cluster signatures to independent datasets.
organization: University of Sheffield; University of Edinburgh

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Three clusters from post-mortem motor-cortex expression were assessed through signature assignment in TargetALS, Italian blood and Dutch blood datasets.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective post-mortem discovery and cross-dataset assignment; clinical utility and prospective classification were not tested.
